info.title: vertexai/imagen-3.0-generate-002
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "vertexai/imagen-3.0-generate-002", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. `x-comfy-router-input-modalities` records the media kinds the model is documented to accept; the request schema is shared across sibling models and may admit media kinds this model ignores. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

instances.prompt: A single red maple leaf on a plain white background.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for the Vertex AI Imagen 3.0 models: the Vertex AI `:predict` response, forwarded unchanged. The operation is DIRECT-RETURN — `routerresult/classification.go` records `{provider: vertexai, endpoint: /imagen/:model}` as `ReturnModeDirect`, metering the original 200 through the synchronous `TrackUsage`, registering no task checker and declaring no status route — so the body a caller receives is the finished generation from the one call. There is no task handle and nothing to poll.
This is NOT the document the Gemini ids on the sibling `/proxy/vertexai/gemini/{model}` route answer, and mixing them up is the one mistake this page exists to prevent. The generated images are in `predictions`, one element per image, with the bytes at `predictions[].bytesBase64Encoded` and the media type at `predictions[].mimeType`. There is no `candidates[]`, no `content.parts[]` and no `inlineData` anywhere in an Imagen response.
Read the ELEMENT field, not the `predictions` container. `ImagenImagePrediction` also carries `prompt`, which is the ENHANCED or rewritten prompt Vertex used rather than output — so an element carrying only a `prompt` is a non-empty array holding no image, exactly as a Kling `videos[]` element with no `url` is.
AN ELEMENT CARRIES ITS IMAGE ONE OF TWO WAYS, and which one you get is decided by the request. By default — `parameters.storageUri` omitted — the image arrives INLINE at `predictions[].bytesBase64Encoded`. Set `parameters.storageUri` to a bucket of your own and Vertex writes the images there instead and names each one at `predictions[].gcsUri`, with no inline bytes. READ WHICHEVER OF THE TWO IS PRESENT. Router does not re-host or rewrite either form: there is no partner URL in this document to replace, a `gcsUri` names the caller's own object and is returned exactly as Vertex wrote it (unsigned, and Comfy grants no access to it), and the inline case is also why `routerresult/classification.go` sizes the row with `BinaryResultMaxBytes` rather than the JSON default.
A `storageUri` naming a COMFY-OWNED bucket is the one destination refused, with a 400, and nothing is generated — see `ImagenImageGenerationParameters.storageUri` for why. `sampleCount` governs how many elements `predictions` carries either way.
The example's `bytesBase64Encoded` is the PLACEHOLDER `PGJhc2U2ND4=`, which decodes to the literal text `<base64>` — a real image would be megabytes, and a real provider response does not belong in a published spec. It is spelled as valid base64 rather than as a bare `<base64>` marker because `ImagenImagePrediction.bytesBase64Encoded` declares `format: byte`, which this document's own example validation enforces.

predictions.prompt: A lighthouse at the edge of the harbour at dawn, warm low sun

storageUri.description:
Optional Cloud Storage destination for the generated images, as a `gs://` URI. When it is set Vertex writes the images there and returns their `gcsUri` instead of inline bytes; when it is omitted the images come back inline as `bytesBase64Encoded`. `ImagenImagePrediction` models both shapes, one field per variant.
IT MUST NAME A BUCKET OF YOUR OWN. This route runs under Comfy's own Google Cloud credentials rather than yours, so a destination inside a Comfy-owned bucket would be a write performed by Comfy's service account, into a shared layout, billed to Comfy's project. A request naming one is refused with a 400 and nothing is generated. Any other destination is forwarded to Vertex unchanged and is yours to grant access to -- Comfy's service account must be able to write to it, or Vertex refuses the generation.

bytesBase64Encoded.description: Base64-encoded image content. Present when the request did NOT set `parameters.storageUri`, which is the default; `gcsUri` takes its place when it did.

gcsUri.description: Cloud Storage URI (`gs://`) of the generated image, present INSTEAD OF `bytesBase64Encoded` when the request set `parameters.storageUri`. The object is written into the bucket the caller named, so reading it is the caller's own business: Router neither re-hosts it onto Comfy storage nor signs it, and the URI is returned exactly as Vertex wrote it.

mimeType.description: MIME type of the generated image

prompt.description: Enhanced or rewritten prompt used to generate this image
